 Though perhaps very obvious, it may be worth mentioning that the convolution identity $\phi=\mu\ast \text{id}$ yields\[\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\phi(n)}{2^n}=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\mu(n)}{(2^n-1)^2}+\frac{1}{2}.\]

 A small related special case is easy to handle. If one keeps only the
terms with \(n=2^m\), one obtains\[
S_2:=\sum_{m\geq 1}\frac{\phi(2^m)}{2^{2^m}}.
\]Since \(\phi(2^m)=2^{m-1}\), this becomes\[
S_2=\sum_{m\geq 1}\frac{2^{m-1}}{2^{2^m}}
 =\sum_{m\geq 1}2^{-(2^m-m+1)}.
\]Thus the binary expansion of \(S_2\) has nonzero digits at positions\[
e_m=2^m-m+1.
\]Moreover\[
e_{m+1}-e_m
=
\bigl(2^{m+1}-(m+1)+1\bigr)-\bigl(2^m-m+1\bigr)
=
2^m-1,
\]so the gaps between successive nonzero binary digits tend to infinity.
If \(S_2\) were rational, its binary expansion would be eventually
periodic. Since \(S_2\) has infinitely many nonzero binary digits,
eventual periodicity would force the gaps between nonzero digits to be
bounded. This contradicts \(e_{m+1}-e_m=2^m-1\to\infty\). Hence\[
\sum_{m\geq 1}\frac{\phi(2^m)}{2^{2^m}}
\]is irrational.
Of course, this does not prove the irrationality of
\(\sum_{n\geq 1}\phi(n)/2^n\), since the omitted terms may create
carries or cancellations. It only shows that the powers-of-two
subseries already contains a simple lacunary irrational component.
 Zeraoulia Rafik
